directive.quote: Every engine job of the old Worker's rust-engine backlog rows works on the new engine, one to one or better.

preserve: calls are counted by sign-in (a personal key, an app's grant, the account's session), never by address
the count is taken when a call arrives, before any of its work runs, with no storage write
the tier is DATA: the first rule whose when holds; an app approved by a weaker way gets the weaker tier (300 calls in 60 seconds), everything else the standard one (1200)
a call past its tier is refused with its words and retry_after_seconds (60), and not counted
the counter holds a bounded number of sign-ins and forgets the oldest first
the connections listing reports each key's and app's limit and how many calls its current window used
a call past its tier is answered HTTP 429 with Retry-After at /mcp (src/mcp.rs too_many_calls_status, old src/sign-in-calls.mjs:39-42), its body the door's refusal unchanged
allowed_deltas: the plan tier (holds access:decision-kept, 3000 calls) and planMarks are dropped: a plan is a product feature (PRINCIPLES 5)
the Cloudflare rate-limiting bindings, their namespace ids and signInCallsBindings drop out (host plumbing, PRINCIPLES 2); the counter lives in the door's memory, a fixed window per sign-in

approved_by is the way the approving session started by, kept on the grant at /authorize/decide (Grant::approved_by), and the weaker rule is stated as approved_by_not [passkey, window]: way names are the account's own rows, so the old kinds email, phone, password and unknown are every approval but a passkey's or the window's
callsWords (the Connections screen line) drops out: screen words are a Workshop tool's
banned_substitutions: a plan or product feature read by the engine
a vendor binding name in engine code
